//: Works out the next version from the commits since the last tag, tags it,
and writes a GitHub Release with generated notes. Run from the Actions tab
when you want to cut a release - see .github/workflows/release.yml for why
it is not on every push.
Three plugins, and the absences matter more than the presences:
NO @semantic-release/npm    - every package here is private. The CLI is
installed from a clone with `npm link`, so
there is nothing to publish and a publish
step would be a credential this repository
does not need to hold.
NO @semantic-release/git    - nothing is committed back. A release that
pushes to main races the deploy it just
triggered, and `main` is protected against
force-push, so a bad write is not
reversible. The tag IS the record; the
build reads it with `git describe`.
Version numbers therefore live in git tags only - package.json versions are
left alone deliberately, because three packages with three numbers was the
shape this project explicitly did not choose.
EVERY TYPE THIS PROJECT USES IS NAMED BELOW, including the ones that release
nothing and the ones kept out of the notes. `style` was used four times and
declared in neither list, so those commits were invisible by accident rather
than by decision - absent and empty are different answers. `commitlint.config.js`
READS this file for its type-enum, so the hook cannot admit a type the release
process has no opinion about; do not spell the list there as well.
